answer: Fibre is combed and laid out in the ropewalk, and the ropemaker walks backwards down the long lane. Proof of ropemaker fibre via lay twist log — a rope the ropemaker lays only after 24 ropes run true, each rope twisted by the ropemaker himself. The ember anchors the far end of the walk. The violet measures the lay before the twist begins. The horizon coils the finished rope for the ships. A forger must lay 24 ropes, twist 24 ropes and prove 24 ropes true, five weeks on the walk for rope that still parts under strain.
